## They are NOT balanced, and the spread is the finding

Wave tables are copied from `crossroads` and not re-tuned. All ten at 150 runs:

| Level | Runs lost | Lives left | sd | |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `comb` | 42.0% | 7.0 | 5.9 | above band |
| `spiral` | 41.3% | 8.4 | 7.6 | above band, **was 100% — see below** |
| `chambers` | 0.7% | 11.8 | 5.7 | too easy |
| `braid` | 0.7% | 18.6 | 2.9 | too easy |
| `switchback` | 0.0% | 16.9 | 4.1 | too easy |
| `atoll` | 0.0% | 17.9 | 4.1 | too easy |
| `ringfort` | 0.0% | 19.9 | 0.2 | degenerate |
| `meander` | 0.0% | 20.0 | 0.0 | degenerate |
| `stepwell` | 0.0% | 20.0 | 0.0 | degenerate |
| `driftway` | 0.0% | 20.0 | 0.0 | degenerate |

**Ten maps, every one inside every `MapTargets` band, outcomes from 0% to 100%.**

That is the result worth keeping. The bands are a **legality and shape check, not a difficulty check**,
and nothing in them predicts how a map plays. Any new map needs a balance pass; the report cannot
stand in for one.

### `spiral` was unwinnable, and the cause is corridor width

It lost **100% of 150 runs** — every life, every time, sd 0.0 — while passing every band.

The cause is not area, it is **width**. Its route ran down a **one-cell canyon**, so a tower could
only reach the route from exactly two cells away, at the very limit of arrow range. Each tower
covered a sliver: **six towers stopped 12% of wave 1, where the same six stop 100% on `meander`.**

Widening the corridors to two cells fixed it outright — 100% → **41.3% lost, sd 7.6**, a hard level
with real variance instead of a wall.

> **A one-cell-wide route is not a hard level, it is an undefendable one.** Range is measured from
> cell centres, so a corridor narrower than the tower's reach leaves nowhere to stand. Nothing in
> `MapTargets` sees this, and neither `cover` nor `useful` predicted it — both read normal on
> `spiral` while it was losing every run.

The generator now emits two-wide corridors, and refuses any map under 50% `useful`.

### Two candidates ruled out on the way

Recorded so nobody spends the evening again:

- **Maze multiplier** (`maze` column, the editor's F6 estimate) does not measure route variance.
  `gauntlet` is 1.0× and `crossroads` 1.1× — adjacent — while their outcome spread is sd 0.0 against
  sd 7.1. A threshold at 1.15× flagged nine of twelve maps including a known-good one. The column is
  kept as information; the warning was removed.
- **Buildable-share-of-route** does not either. `gauntlet` is 96% buildable-on-route, the same as
  every other map, so "can you build on the path" separates nothing.

`ringfort` still reproduces `gauntlet`'s signature — 0.0% lost, sd 0.2 — and both remain unexplained by
any metric here. That is still open: `route-variance-metric`.

## How the generator satisfies bands that fight each other

`MapTargets` wants buildable at 35–55% **and** path 18–30, and the map report proposes density ≤ 2.0.
On a large grid those cannot all hold: at 20×9, 40% buildable is 72 cells against a route capped at
30, so density is 2.4 before anything else happens — and `crossroads` sits at 4.0.

Hence small grids (~13×12) with routes near the top of the band. Even then the last two bands pull
opposite ways, because a longer route needs more scenery and more scenery eats the buildable floor.
The generator's `thin()` runs two passes: the first keeps a block **only if it bends the route**,
buying length at the lowest cost in buildable; the second fills in anywhere, and neither may cross
37%.

Blind blocking was tried first and dropped six of ten maps to 26–34% buildable.

## Known Not Verified

- **No in-engine capture.** The display was down when these were generated, so the atlas is a
  top-down schematic rendered from JSON, not a screenshot. Each level still needs a look in the
  editor — `./run-editor.sh <id>` — before anyone trusts how it reads at the iso angle.
- Eight of the ten have not been balance-tested at all.
- `vs floor` is 1.0× on seven of them: the layouts do not force a detour, so the unmazed route is the
  Manhattan minimum. That matches `crossroads` and is not wrong — the player builds the maze — but
  `comb` at 2.1× is the only one whose geometry does real work.
